problem: Writing 'a zero at −z rad/s, a pole at −p rad/s' mixes a point on the s-plane with a frequency. A student may read it as a zero at a negative frequency instead of at s = −z.
fix: Say the zero is at s = −z and the pole at s = −p, with z and p (the corner frequencies) in rad/s and p > z.

problem: The step says to read the uncompensated gain crossover but never uses it. The formula φm = PMreq − PMold + δ quietly assumes the plant phase at the new crossover is close to the plant phase at the old crossover, with δ absorbing the difference. A student may think the formula is exact.
fix: Add one sentence: the formula assumes the plant phase at the new crossover ωm is close to the phase at the old crossover; δ covers the shift, and if the crossover moves a long way the plant phase at ωm must be recomputed.

problem: 'The closed-loop characteristic equation is s²+4s+16=0' drops the cancelled factor. Before cancellation the loop characteristic polynomial is (s+2)(s²+4s+16), so the pole at −2 remains a closed-loop mode unless the zero-pole cancellation is exact.
fix: Say: after the exact cancellation the loop reduces to 16/[s(s+4)], whose characteristic equation is s²+4s+16=0; the cancelled pole at −2 stays as a mode in the physical system.
